rulings.topic: A quotation before its verb of saying
rulings.ruling: A direct quotation may come before its verb of saying, closed by a comma inside the quotation marks: “…,” saivo po senosia. It may also follow its verb after a colon (2.3:G83). The quotation is its own sentence or sentences; the clause around it is read without it.
settles_open_questions: Speech before its verb of saying (the draft's G-9).

rulings.ruling: Two or more adjectives before one noun stand in this order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose. With more than three, put one in a raho clause.
examples: Saivo po vimova baba vanisan nolsasan kadu.
She saw a beautiful new car.
Li lira raho ka molusan ka vanisan.
The song, which is gentle, is beautiful.
settles_open_questions: The order of two or more adjectives before one noun (A4.22, I-28).

rulings.ruling: A duration is en + NUMBER + a time noun after the verb: en dossa deya, for two days. en rinbakrono (3.0:G139) is its unbounded case.
examples: Maivo po lisrola en dossa deya.
settles_open_questions: A duration (“for two days”) in general (I-17).

rulings.ruling: An action is compared with la kasi (or la menu) + an adjective + tamo X: Maivo lirala la kasi benasan tamo taivo, I sing better than you. With no adjective, use benasan (well) or mellisan (much).
examples: Maivo lirala la kasi benasan tamo taivo.
settles_open_questions: Comparing an action with no manner adjective (“I sing more than you”).

rulings.ruling: “Destined to” is fatofa sidu + verb: Saivo fatofa sidu lirala. ke sidu is not used for destiny.
settles_open_questions: ke sidu VERB as “destined to” (album 08): fatofa sidu instead.

rulings.ruling: A decimal or a percentage is said as a fraction, NUMBER de NUMBER (trezira-penta de centa, thirty-five per cent), or rounded.
examples: Trezira-penta de centa nelari po lirala.
Thirty-five per cent of the people sang.
